## 💡 Why this exists

> "*If you don't practice, you won't learn anything.*"
> — the epigraph of [R4DEV's practice page](https://r4dev.netlify.app/sessions_tools/09-practice/09-practice.html). Still true.

Most of us use AI the same way every time: ask, copy, paste, repeat tomorrow. The asking got easy. The doing didn't.

Claude Code closes that gap. It turns everyday requests — "summarize these files," "build me a slide deck," "review this strategy" — into workflows you save once and run forever. *From asking to doing* is a hands-on introduction for Jacobs Foundation staff on working with it productively and reliably.

I built [R4DEV](https://r4dev.netlify.app/) to teach R to my constantly rotating team with the same philosophy; word got around and over 80 people joined. The lesson from that experience carried over here: nobody learns a tool from a manual. You learn by watching someone solve a real problem, then trying it on one of yours.

## 🦾 How it's structured

- **[Motivation](intro.qmd)**: Why use Claude Code, no coding background needed.
- **[Session 0 · Setup](session-0.qmd)**: Install a terminal, Git, and Claude Code before Session 1.
- **[Session 1 · Slidemaking](01_slidemaker/session-1.qmd)**: Introduction to Claude Code and skills.
- **[Session 2 · Mixing it up](02_summarizer/session-2.qmd)**: Introduction to workflows.
- **[Session 3 · Extended Team](03_multitudes/session-3.qmd)**: Multi-agent review workflow.

Between sessions, the **[Thesaurus](thesaurus.qmd)** defines the terms, the
**[Skills](skill-collection.qmd)** and **[Agents](agent-collection.qmd)**
collections catalog what was built, and **[Tips](tips.qmd)** collects what the
decks keep repeating.

## 📦 Replicating a session

Every session is a folder you can download from its page and open directly in
Claude Code or Codex. Inside you will find `README.md` (the human quickstart),
`CLAUDE.md` (the defaults Claude reads), `AGENTS.md` (the same for Codex), the
runnable skills under `.claude/skills/`, and the sample inputs. Run the slash
command on the sample, then on your own files.

The folders are maintained in the open at
[nelsonamayad-jf/from-asking-to-doing](https://github.com/nelsonamayad-jf/from-asking-to-doing).
Only validated sessions are published there; the website's own source is
[nelsonamayad-jf/from-asking-to-doing-site](https://github.com/nelsonamayad-jf/from-asking-to-doing-site).
